clips.title: Social Security 2027 COLA: your new check at $1,500, $2,000, $3,000 #Shorts
Medicare takes about $6.60 of your 2027 Social Security raise #Shorts
clips.desc: 3.6% COLA minus the projected 2027 Part B increase ($202.90 → $209.50, Medicare Trustees; official figure due in November). Our calculation.

shots.title: Social Security, January 2027
shots.src: Social Security Administration · 2027 COLA Fact Sheet and ssa.gov/cola (COLA 3.6%, payable January 2027)

stats.at: two thousand one hundred and seventy
stats.label: average retired worker, after

shots.narration: Three point six percent. {p} Starting with the payment you get in January, every Social Security check goes up by three point six percent. That's the official cost-of-living adjustment for 2027. {p} For the average retired worker, the check goes from about two thousand ninety-five dollars to about two thousand one hundred and seventy. Seventy-five dollars more a month. {pp} But if your Medicare premium comes out of that check, you won't see all seventy-five. {p} So in this video: your new check at every common benefit level, exactly how much Medicare takes back, who pays more, and the other numbers that change on January first.

Everything here comes from the Social Security Administration's own fact sheet and from Medicare's published figures. Where a number is still a projection, I'll say so. {p} And the usual reminder: this is education, not financial advice. <soft>Let's start with the number you actually came for.</soft>

shots.title: Your check after the 3.6% COLA
shots.src: Social Security Administration · 2027 COLA Fact Sheet and ssa.gov/cola (COLA 3.6%, payable January 2027) · Nest Egg Atlas calculation
shots.narration: Here's the math, before Medicare. {p} If your check is a thousand dollars today, it becomes about one thousand thirty-six. Thirty-six dollars more. {p} At fifteen hundred: about fifteen fifty-four. Fifty-four more. {p} At two thousand dollars, the most common range: about two thousand seventy-two. Seventy-two dollars more. {p} At twenty-five hundred: twenty-five ninety. Ninety more. {p} At three thousand: three thousand one hundred and eight. A hundred and eight more. {p} And at four thousand, close to the maximum: four thousand one hundred forty-four. A hundred and forty-four more. {pp} One detail: Social Security rounds the final amount down to the whole dollar, so your exact figure may come out a dollar lower than these.

The percentage is the same for everyone, so the bigger your check, the bigger your raise in dollars. {p} Three point six percent of a small check is a small number. That's how a cost-of-living adjustment works: it protects the buying power you already have. It doesn't close the gap between a small benefit and a large one. {p} Now for the part that surprises people every January.

shots.title: Medicare Part B, standard premium
shots.src: Medicare Part B: 2026 premium $202.90 (CMS) · 2027 premium $209.50 PROJECTED by the Medicare Trustees (official figure due in November)

stats.at: two hundred two dollars and ninety
stats.label: 2026, per month (CMS)

shots.narration: Most retirees pay their Medicare Part B premium straight out of their Social Security check. {p} In 2026, the standard premium is two hundred two dollars and ninety cents a month. {p} For 2027, Medicare's trustees project about two hundred nine fifty. That's six dollars and sixty cents more a month. The yearly deductible is projected to go from two hundred eighty-three dollars to about two hundred ninety-two. {pp} I'm saying projected on purpose: the official number comes from Medicare in November and can land a little above or below this. If the projection holds, here's your raise after Medicare.

shots.title: Your raise after the Part B increase
shots.sub: Extra dollars per month, January 2027 · projected Part B
shots.src: Social Security Administration · 2027 COLA Fact Sheet and ssa.gov/cola (COLA 3.6%, payable January 2027) · Medicare Part B: 2026 premium $202.90 (CMS) · 2027 premium $209.50 PROJECTED by the Medicare Trustees (official figure due in November) · Nest Egg Atlas calculation
shots.narration: On a thousand-dollar check, the thirty-six dollar raise becomes about twenty-nine forty after Medicare. {p} At fifteen hundred, fifty-four becomes about forty-seven forty. {p} At two thousand, seventy-two becomes about sixty-five forty. {p} At three thousand, a hundred and eight becomes about a hundred and one forty. {p} And at four thousand, a hundred forty-four becomes about a hundred thirty-seven forty. {pp} So Medicare takes back about six and a half dollars of everyone's raise. On a small check, that's almost a fifth of it. On a big check, it's barely noticeable.

One protection worth knowing: a rule called hold harmless. Your net check can't go down because of a Part B increase. {p} With a three point six percent COLA, that only matters for checks under about a hundred and eighty-five dollars, so it won't come into play for almost anyone this year. {p} Some people, though, pay a lot more than the standard premium.

items.text: Hold harmless: net check can't fall

shots.title: Who pays more than the standard premium
shots.src: CMS · 2026 income-related monthly adjustment amounts (IRMAA), based on 2024 tax returns
shots.narration: Not everyone pays the standard premium. {p} If your income is above a certain level, Medicare adds a surcharge called IRMAA. {p} For 2026, that starts at a hundred and nine thousand dollars of modified adjusted gross income for a single filer, or two hundred eighteen thousand for a couple filing jointly. {p} At that first tier, the Part B premium jumps from two hundred two ninety to two hundred eighty-four ten a month. Higher tiers pay more again. {p} And here's the detail that catches people: Medicare looks at your tax return from two years earlier. Your 2027 premium is based on your 2025 income. {pp} The 2027 brackets will be published with the premium announcement. If you sold a house, took a big withdrawal, or converted an IRA in 2025, this is the year it shows up.

Quick favor before the next part: if you find this useful, subscribe. Retirement money, in real numbers, from the official sources, every week. {p} Now, where does three point six percent come from, and is it a lot?

items.at: three point six percent come from

shots.narration: The COLA is set by law. It's the rise in a consumer price index for workers, comparing the third quarter of this year with the third quarter of last year. No vote, no politics, just the formula. {p} Here's every COLA since 2000. {p} Most years sit between one and three percent. The average over this whole period is about two point six. {p} There were three years with zero: 2010, 2011, and 2016. {p} And then 2022 and 2023, when inflation spiked: five point nine percent, then eight point seven, the biggest since 1981. {pp} Three point six percent for 2027 is the highest since 2023, and well above the average. That's not great news, in a way: it means prices rose faster this year than last.

shots.title: Other Social Security numbers for 2027
shots.src: Social Security Administration · 2027 COLA Fact Sheet and ssa.gov/cola (COLA 3.6%, payable January 2027)
shots.narration: A few other numbers change on January first, and some of them matter more than the COLA. {p} If you're still working and under full retirement age, you can earn up to twenty-five thousand five hundred and sixty dollars in 2027 before Social Security withholds anything. Above that, it holds back one dollar for every two you earn. {p} In the year you reach full retirement age, the limit is sixty-seven thousand nine hundred and twenty, and the penalty drops to one dollar for every three. {p} Once you reach full retirement age, there's no limit at all. And money withheld under this test isn't lost: Social Security recalculates your benefit at full retirement age to give credit for it. {p} The maximum benefit for someone retiring at full retirement age rises to four thousand one hundred eighty-eight dollars a month. {p} The maximum amount of wages taxed for Social Security goes to a hundred ninety-two thousand three hundred. {p} And SSI, the separate program for people with very low income, rises to one thousand twenty-nine dollars a month for an individual, with the increase arriving on December thirty-first.

items.text: SSI increase: Dec 31 · Social Security: January

shots.title: Taxes on your benefit
shots.src: IRS · combined income thresholds ($25,000/$32,000 and $34,000/$44,000, not indexed) · 2025 law: extra $6,000 deduction for 65+ (2025–2028)

stats.label: single: benefits start being taxed (combined income)
maximum share of benefits that is taxable

shots.narration: One more thing a raise can do: push more of your benefit into taxable territory. {p} Whether your Social Security is taxed depends on your combined income: your other income, plus half your benefits. For a single person, taxation starts above twenty-five thousand dollars. For a couple, above thirty-two thousand. Up to eighty-five percent of your benefit can be taxable. {p} Those thresholds were set decades ago and have never been adjusted for inflation, so every COLA pulls a few more people across the line. {pp} The good news: the tax law passed in July 2025 added an extra six thousand dollar deduction for people sixty-five and older, for tax years 2025 through 2028. It shrinks above seventy-five thousand dollars of income, or a hundred and fifty thousand for couples. For many retirees, it more than cancels the tax on their benefits.

So, the bottom line. {p} Your check goes up three point six percent in January. On a two thousand dollar benefit, that's seventy-two dollars, and about sixty-five after the projected Medicare increase. {p} Watch your mailbox or your online account in late November: Social Security sends every beneficiary a notice with the exact new amount, and in December, the amount after Medicare. {pp} <soft>What's your number? Tell me in the comments whether your raise covers what your costs did this year.</soft>
If you want to see how your check was calculated in the first place, from your salary, with the 2027 formula, watch this next. {p} This is Nest Egg Atlas. See you next time.

yt.title: Social Security COLA 2027: Your New Check at $1,500, $2,000, $3,000 (After Medicare Part B)
yt.description:
The 2027 Social Security COLA is 3.6%, payable with the January 2027 check. We show the new monthly benefit at $1,000, $1,500, $2,000, $2,500, $3,000 and $4,000, how much the projected 2027 Medicare Part B premium ($209.50, Medicare Trustees; official figure due in November) takes back, the IRMAA income surcharge, why the COLA is 3.6%, every COLA since 2000, the other 2027 numbers (earnings test, taxable maximum, maximum benefit, SSI), and how benefits are taxed.

Educational content, not financial advice.

Sources: Social Security Administration, 2027 COLA Fact Sheet and ssa.gov/cola; CMS, 2026 Medicare Parts A & B premiums and deductibles; 2026 Medicare Trustees Report (2027 Part B projection); IRS (taxation of benefits); Public Law 119-21 (senior deduction). Calculations: Nest Egg Atlas.
